objective: Provide password confirmation at signup and Cognito verification-code recovery for email-verified accounts, with an Account details entry point and a static email-verification disclaimer.
acceptance_criteria: RESEARCH/IMPLEMENTATION STOP GATE: ADR 0009 (wiki/GeneralContext/Decisions/0009-account-lifecycle-evidence.md), its linked evidence/failure matrix and proof plan replace the provisional cutoff contract. Merge this human-reviewed Director amendment first. Its merge alone does NOT release AUTH-001: authoritative lost/late provider completion and revocation evidence, or another human-reviewed architecture amendment, plus exact scope/IAM prerequisites must merge before any implementation resumes or a dependent AUTH-001 PR opens. Neither timer unlocking nor manual-only recovery is approved.

Completed prerequisites: USERS-006/007 deployed; Director IAM PR #370 deployed with exact-pool AdminGetUser and AdminUserGlobalSignOut grants and boundary v3 verified. Scope PRs #375/#376 merged. Do not repeat completed AWS writes. These prerequisites do not release the research/provider proof stop gate or cover new worker roles/IAM/scope.

Scope gate: keep this allowed_paths and guard policy unchanged during research. Lifecycle facade, module consumers, token transport, trigger/queue/reconciler, IAM and deployment changes identified in the proof plan need their own precise human-reviewed Director scope/spec prerequisites before test-first implementation. No task worker may widen .ai/policy.json or its own specification.

The sign-in page retains an accessible Forgot password link below the password field. The request page contains a labelled email input, a confirm button, and a static disclaimer that users must verify their email before resetting their password. The code-entry page has labelled code, New password, and Confirm password inputs.

For every syntactically valid request, known, unknown, disabled, and unverified addresses receive the same success status, body, and user-facing message, with no account-existence, verification, or delivery detail. Only an email-verified account can receive a recovery code, delivered by Cognito's existing default email sender to its verified_email recovery method. Unverified accounts receive no code. The app does not rely on SES or a custom sender for recovery. Reset does not set email_verified.
Requests are rate-limited by normalized account address and source IP to at most 5 requests per hour per key. Unknown, disabled, and unverified-account cases do not reveal which case occurred.

Recovery uses Cognito ForgotPassword and ConfirmForgotPassword verification-code operations only. Cognito owns code expiry, single-use, and attempt controls. The app does not create custom reset links or app-issued reset tokens, persist or log recovery codes, or maintain reset-token records.

Candidate confirmation boundary, not implementation authorization: use native Cognito ConfirmForgotPassword with transient code/password only. Record an application operation before external work, but do not lock, revoke or modify an account because an unauthenticated request or invalid code arrived. The current public app client permits direct provider calls; backend ownership is not an enforceable sole-entry guarantee. Resolve bypass, entirely lost completion evidence and late completion in the separate provider proof gate.

New password and confirmation must match before submission. A mismatch is an accessible field error and makes no Cognito confirmation call. Cognito rejects invalid, expired, consumed, or exhausted codes without changing the password; the app does not expose account details.

The sign-up form has labelled Password and Confirm password fields. A mismatch is an accessible field error and makes no Cognito SignUp request; matching values submit once. Optional email verification behavior remains unchanged.

If the signed-in user navigates to the password-recovery route, the app signs them out and clears the active session before exposing a form that can submit a recovery request or password change. A test proves that no recovery request is sent before sign-out completes.

Account settings begins with an Account details section. It shows the signed-in user's email in an Email row and a Password row with a Reset password button instead of a password value. The button opens the same password-recovery route used from sign-in.

Durable lifecycle authority is proposed by ADR 0009: immutable issuer/pool plus Cognito sub, independent of profile lifetime; monotonic generations, inactive/deleting/deleted states and deletion dominance. Every identity path, including profile creation and no-profile retry, must consult it and fail closed on lookup failure. Deletion/tombstone and cross-module paths require separate reviewed Director scope prerequisites; this task does not authorize edits outside allowed_paths.

Use durable operation identifiers, owner or hashed random capability-authorized generic status, idempotency, atomic local outbox/inbox, fenced workers and automatic reconciliation of known unfinished stages. Do not persist/log/queue codes or passwords, or automatically replay confirmation from stored secrets. A timeout, code mismatch after retry, new login, elapsed time, UserLastModifiedDate or lease expiry does not prove an earlier provider call ended. provider_unknown is not success and must not become an unauthenticated account lock.

Evaluate PostConfirmation_ConfirmForgotPassword as positive completion evidence, not atomic/durable/exactly-once delivery. Preserve existing triggers; restrict invocation to the exact pool/account and bind immutable sub independently of untrusted ClientMetadata. Handle missing, duplicated, replayed and out-of-order events, and direct provider confirmation without metadata. A queue/outbox only reconciles durably received work; an entirely lost hook remains a release blocker until the independent enforcement/evidence gate is resolved. Serialize revocation retries and never admit sessions merely because a timer or lease elapsed.

Before release prove the ADR 0009 failure matrix and ordered proof plan: rollback/crash/late completion at every external and database boundary; no invalid-code account lock; trusted-source/sub correlation; secret redaction including validation failures; operation/status enumeration resistance; durable tombstone anti-resurrection and recover/delete/mutation races; automatic recovery of known work; token liveness and locally verified revoked JWT rejection at the selected enforcement boundary. GetUser online access-token validation and managed sessions are evaluated defences, not reset-completion evidence. Native-code UX, request equivalence/rate limits, password mismatch, pre-recovery sign-out and static reminder remain required. Browser/provider rows require explicit dev-write approval and report evidence or NOT DONE; finite empirical timing tests cannot prove a provider guarantee.
No new dependency. The relevant Users and Frontend module references record the flow and its security boundary.
